children: EQUITY SUPPLY GLUT FLASHES WARNING FOR AI RALLY

The AI-led equity rally may be entering its final phase as the flood of new shares meets weakening investor appetite, and Anthropic’s initial public offering this week will be a key test of demand, according to Capital Economics.
US equity issuance surged this year, and net equity issuance hit a record high in the second quarter, aided by SpaceX's record IPO and share sales by several AI hyperscalers.

But historically, periods of positive net issuance have often coincided with market peaks, as companies seize elevated valuations and the rising supply of stock begins to overwhelm demand, said Joe Maher, markets economist at the firm.
More recent data also point to a slowdown. US share issuance has retreated since a summer burst, while the IPO market has cooled sharply following SpaceX's June listing.

Anthropic's flotation will offer the clearest measure of whether investors remain willing to fund AI companies at extraordinary valuations. The company could raise up to $100 billion, including private placements, a record that surpasses SpaceX's haul. Yet its reported valuation target has already been cut to roughly $1.3 trillion to $1.5 trillion from $2 trillion.

The stakes extend beyond Anthropic. Major cloud providers and chipmakers are among its backers, underlining the increasingly circular financing of the AI ecosystem. A strong debut could lift AI shares temporarily, but ultimately prove short-lived.
“Equity issuance is one of several late-cycle indicators that are flashing red and make us think that the AI boom is in its final stages,” Maher said.
